prerequisites: Sufficient knowledge of the English language for practical work with software and understanding some readings.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Students know how to apply acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.
Students possess learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.

Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urban planning and infrastructures.
Project, calculate and design products, processes, facilities and plants.
Direct, plan and supervise multidisciplinary teams.
Perform strategic planning and apply it to both constructive and production, quality and environmental management systems.
Manage technically and economically projects, facilities, plants, companies and technological centers.
Be able to exercise general management, technical management and R&D&I project management functions in plants, companies and technological centers.
Ability to design and project automated production systems and advanced process control.
Knowledge and skills to organize and manage companies.
Knowledge and skills in strategy and planning applied to different organizational structures.
Knowledge of management information systems, industrial organization, production and logistics systems and quality management systems.
Use digital simulation techniques as an aid in developing management skills and in the analysis of production and logistics systems.
Be able to apply discrete event-oriented system modeling methods.
Be able to use some of the most commonly employed simulation software programs both at research and company level.

syllabus_topics: Simulation as a tool for the development of management capabilities in the company.
Simulation of business strategies. Simulation of production and logistics processes.
Business Management Simulation. Using a business game, the decision-making process and the analysis of the results obtained are experimented.
Problem solving using simulation as an analysis tool
Construction of simulation models of production and/or logistics systems

assessment_methods.method: Timed Control (CP1) - Written test on theoretical part (manual Monte Carlo simulation)
Timed Control (CP2) - Practical test on building and validating a simple Arena simulation model
Individual Tasks (TI) - Resolution of exercises using simulation (Excel and Arena)
Final Individual Project (TIF) - Resolution of two cases using simulation, including documentation and public presentation

assessment_rules: The ordinary evaluation includes CP1 (max 1.5 points), CP2 (max 1.5 points), Individual Tasks TI (max 2 points), and a Final Individual Project TIF (max 5 points). A minimum score of 1 point is required for the sum of CP1+CP2+TI, and a minimum of 2 points for TIF. If all minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as NOTA = CP1 + CP2 + TI + TIF. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, CP1 and CP2 scores are kept, TI tasks can be redone, and the TIF must be submitted.
